citation: Chang et al. 2026. Phylotranscriptomics and genome-size evidence clarify the Taiwanese Cirsium japonicum complex and delimit C. brevicaule and allied East Asian thistles
coverage: 37 samples total; 33 Cirsium samples; Taiwan/Ryukyu/Japan focal sampling
usable_for: nuclear species-tree scaffold; lineage delimitation; leaf-transcriptome coding-integrity screen; verified visible corolla states
not_usable_for: petal expression; pigment chemistry; causal pollinator inference
notes: RNA was sampled from fresh leaves. Publication reports Illumina NovaSeq but current SRA RunInfo says Illumina MiniSeq for all 25 focal runs; preserve as unresolved provenance conflict. SRA ScientificName is also coarse/mismatched for 18/25 runs, so downstream taxon identity must use audited sample/voucher mapping.

citation: Fan et al. 2026. Transposable Element-Mediated Structural Variation Drives Flower Colour Diversification in Camellia
coverage: 237 accessions; 11 de novo genomes; major Camellia flower-colour types
usable_for: published nuclear phylogenetic framework; visible-colour ancestral reconstruction; TE/SV regulatory mechanism; MYB60 anthocyanin-suppression evidence
not_usable_for: independent raw-data reanalysis; treating the published tree as a locally reproduced result
notes: The paper's Data Availability Statement says supporting data are available on request from the corresponding author and are not publicly available. Treat its white-MRCA reconstruction and 237-accession topology as published evidence, not a reproduced project result.

citation: Fan et al. 2026. A near telomere-to-telomere genome reveals yellow camellias evolution and flavonols biosynthesis
coverage: 79 accessions; 26 yellow Camellia from China; 18 from Vietnam; Camellia longruiensis gap-free phased genome
usable_for: published yellow-lineage nuclear phylogeny; China-Vietnam comparison; C. cucphuongensis/C. flava distinct trajectory; WRKY23-to-FLS regulatory evidence
not_usable_for: independent raw-data reanalysis; treating the 79-accession tree as a locally reproduced result
notes: The article's Data availability statement says data will be made available on request. Most yellow accessions form a major lineage while C. cucphuongensis and C. flava follow a distinct trajectory; these remain published results until sequence/tree inputs are obtained.

citation: Zhou et al. 2013. Functional analyses of a flavonol synthase-like gene from Camellia nitidissima reveal its roles in flavonoid metabolism during floral pigmentation
usable_for: taxon-specific CnFLS1 function; flavonol accumulation; experimental flux competition with anthocyanin
notes: CnFLS1 overexpression in tobacco increased flavonols, reduced anthocyanins, and shifted flowers toward white/light yellow.

citation: Zhou et al. 2017. De novo Assembly of the Camellia nitidissima Transcriptome Reveals Key Genes of Flower Pigment Biosynthesis
coverage: five flower developmental stages; 15 flower samples
usable_for: public petal/flower RNA-seq; HPLC pigment evidence; carotenoid and flavonol pathway expression
notes: Golden-yellow petals contain both carotenoids and flavonol glycosides. Publication and SRA agree on HiSeq 2500 and total yield. BioSample dev_stage metadata resolves archive groups 10/6/7/8/9 to biological stages S1/S2/S3/S4/S5, with three biological replicates each; the frozen mapping is in data/camellia_srp112181_admitted_manifest_v0_1.csv.

citation: Feng et al. 2024. Multi-omics analysis revealed the mechanism underlying flavonol biosynthesis during petal color formation in Camellia nitidissima
usable_for: CnFLS2 petal expression; flavonol/anthocyanin developmental contrast; transient overexpression; JA-CnFLS2 regulation
not_usable_for: genus-wide transition history; public reanalysis until raw accession is verified
notes: Flavonols rise during golden-petal formation while several anthocyanin/proanthocyanidin signals decline; CnFLS2 overexpression increases flavonol content.

citation: Wang et al. 2025. A telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of Camellia nitidissima
usable_for: public chromosome-scale yellow-Camellia reference; anthocyanin/flavonol/carotenoid pathway coding inventory; regulatory-neighbourhood inspection
notes: 2.72-Gb, 15-pseudochromosome T2T reference with 35,701 protein-coding genes; raw genomic and RNA data are deposited in NGDC and assembly is also available through NCBI/NGDC.

citation: Lv et al. 2025. Near telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of Camellia pitardii
usable_for: public non-yellow comparative Camellia genome; coding-pathway comparison; regulatory-neighbourhood comparison
notes: Public near-T2T genome with eight gap-free chromosomes; useful as an independent white-to-rose-pink comparative genome rather than as a substitute for the inaccessible 2026 population datasets.

citation: Xie et al. 2025. Phylotranscriptomics resolved phylogenetic relationships and divergence time between 20 golden camellia species
coverage: 20 named golden Camellia accessions/species; original habitats mainly Guangxi with one Northeast Vietnam accession
public_accession: SRR27212615-SRR27212634 (non-numeric table order; exact mapping frozen separately)
usable_for: public yellow-lineage nuclear transcriptomic backbone; coding-pathway comparison; public C. longruiensis RNA-seq; China-Vietnam yellow comparison
not_usable_for: petal expression; assuming each published species name is an independent lineage; reliable divergence-time inference
notes: All 20 leaf transcriptomes are public as individual SRR accessions. The paper itself says exact golden-Camellia species number is uncertain and calls its divergence-time conclusions tentative because the molecular-clock assumption failed. Taxonomic independence must be re-audited before counting colour origins.

citation: Liu et al. 2025. Species concept of golden flower camellias in China
coverage: 95 newly sampled ITS; 65 newly determined plastomes; combined ITS 931 sequences/160 Camellia taxa and plastid 322 genomes/140 taxa
usable_for: taxonomic-independence audit; hybridization/chloroplast-capture flags; Chinese golden-Camellia species circumscription
not_usable_for: single nuclear species tree; direct pigment mechanism; treating chloroplast topology as species history
notes: Recognizes about 23 golden-flower Camellia species in China and documents extensive hybridization/chloroplast capture. Critically, C. longgangensis and C. longruiensis are treated as synonyms of C. flavida; C. longzhouensis is not a clean independent species and may involve C. chrysanthoides-related variation/hybrid origin. Use this source as a gate before treating the 20 transcriptome names as independent evolutionary units.
